doc: Host-level corpus (gate p2-hostile-host). Each case maps to exactly one invariant id (SPEC_INVARIANTS H). The real aegis binary (feature p2) is booted with an oracle-written F8 config: one route + module per case, run under p2.isolation = forkwasm and = cordon. worker: real = the --worker binary; escaped = the oracle's compromised worker (reference worker with HOSTILE_ESCAPED=1), which forwards whatever the module emits, so the supervisor's own decoder is judged. cap: all = select/insert/update/delete/upsert on notes(id, body); ro = select only; none = no data key. expect: allow (200 + exact body + the module header, host framing) | deny (status and body identical to the explicit-Deny response of h-control-deny, non-2xx, and none of `absent` anywhere in the raw response bytes) | any. Placeholders in args: {rowid} = this case's unique row id, {victim} = the victim tenant (u64). effect: own_rows = rows of this case's tenant after the request; rowid_rows = rows with this case's row id under any tenant. audit: allow / deny_min = F9 events with action p2.data_run, actor.tenant = this case's tenant.

cases.doc: Vacuity: an Allow completion reaches the client re-serialized by the host.
Explicit Deny: the host's fixed response; it defines the deny response every failure case must equal.
Vacuity: an authorized data_run reaches SQLite under the route-bound tenant and is audited once.
Route without data capability (INV-NONEMPTY): the op is refused with the uniform error result, audited as refused, no effect.
insert on a select-only capability: refused, no effect.
A collection outside the route's CapSet: refused.
A write to a column outside the capability's columns: refused.
A write to the tenant column (F4 TenantFieldWritten): refused.
Effective-context switch: the op names the victim tenant; the supervisor overwrites it with the route-bound tenant, so the row lands under the caller's tenant only.
A select naming the victim tenant returns none of the victim's rows.
An op that fails the F10 decoder: decode failure (worker killed, principal charged), host deny response, no effect.
A filter nested 200 deep (> F4 MAX_PRED_DEPTH = 64): decode failure before constructing, deny.
42 KB of body (several resp-body frames) then a trap: nothing the module wrote reaches the client.
Header value with CR LF (response splitting): rejected, never repaired.
Bare LF in a header value: rejected.
NUL in a header value: rejected.
obs-text (0xE9) in a header value (CVE-2026-73552 pattern): rejected.
Invalid UTF-8 bytes in a header value: rejected.
A non-lower-case header name: rejected (not lower-cased).
A header name that is not an RFC 9110 token: rejected.
Trailing whitespace in a header value: rejected (not trimmed).
A module-authored framing field: rejected (framing is host-computed).
transfer-encoding from a module: rejected.
A hop-by-hop field: rejected.
200 header fields > limits.max_header_fields (128): rejected.
Summed header size 20,740 > limits.max_header_list_size (16,384): rejected.
resp_head twice (double response): trap, deny.
A status outside 200..599 (101 Switching Protocols): rejected.
Compromised worker forwards a CR LF header: the supervisor's re-check rejects it (decode failure); no module byte reaches the client.
Compromised worker forwards obs-text: rejected by the supervisor.
Compromised worker forwards transfer-encoding: rejected by the supervisor.
Compromised worker forwards status 101: rejected by the supervisor.
Compromised worker sends two resp-head frames for one req-id: decode failure, deny.
After resp-end(trap) the compromised worker sends a late resp-head/resp-body/resp-end(0) for the finished req-id: never forwarded.
A 70,000-byte resp-body frame (> frame_max_bytes 65,536): decode failure, deny.
The oracle holds the SQLite write lock while the request runs: the p2.data_run audit event must already be in the log while the effect is still blocked; after release the row appears.
data_run then trap: the authorized op stays audited although the request failed; no row exists without its audit event.
handle() returns 7 (Error): Deny.
handle() returns 0xFFFFFFFF: Error => Deny.
A trap before any output: Deny.
A complete response followed by a trap: the trap decides (Deny), the response is discarded.
Response written, then an infinite loop: the wall bound ends it and the host denies within wall_ms + grace.
D7: three trapping requests from one principal, then that principal's next request (to a healthy route) gets 429; another principal's request to the healthy route still gets 200.
